title: Methods of experimental study of thermal convection in cavity subject to rotation and vibration
author: Kozlov, Vjatkin, et al.

steps.title: Set outer boundary temperature
steps.instruction: Set the temperature of the outer cylinder wall (T3) to 19–22 °C using a thermostat and maintain it constant.

steps.title: Establish uniform cavity temperature
steps.instruction: Allow the cavity to reach a constant uniform temperature before proceeding.

steps.title: Calibrate temperature sensors
steps.instruction: Calibrate the integral‑resistance thermometers (sensors T1 and T2) after the uniform temperature is achieved.

steps.title: Start rotation and apply AC voltage
steps.instruction: Drive the cuvette at a rotation speed up to 4 rps, connect the electrodes to the AC source APS‑9501 and set the desired alternating voltage.

steps.title: Reach steady‑state temperature distribution
steps.instruction: Continue rotating at the chosen constant speed while the heat released in the liquid warms it; rotation distributes the heat so the maximum temperature occurs on the cylinder axis. Monitor T1 and T2; this stage typically lasts 1–3 h depending on the solution and heat‑release power.

steps.title: Convection experiment without vibrations
steps.instruction: Perform the experiment in a rotating horizontal cavity with no external vibrations.

steps.title: Decrease rotation speed stepwise
steps.instruction: Reduce the rotational velocity of the cavity in discrete steps, recording temperature data at each step.

substeps.instruction: Use a default step size of 0.1 rps.
If the current speed > 1.2 rps and sensor readings change little, increase the step to 0.2 rps.
If the speed is in the developed‑convection region (≈ 0.7 rps), decrease the step to 0.05 rps.

steps.title: Allow convection to stabilize
steps.instruction: After each speed change, wait 10–60 min for a stationary convection mode before recording data.

steps.title: Record temperature data
steps.instruction: Collect T1 and T2 readings at a sampling frequency of 1 s⁻¹ for the duration of the stationary period; if temperature fluctuations appear, extend the recording time to capture several full periods of oscillation.

steps.title: Process temperature records
steps.instruction: When analysing the data, use only the portions recorded after the stationary convection mode has been reached, discarding the transient spin‑down interval.

steps.title: Calculate average temperatures and ΔT
steps.instruction: For each stationary step, compute the time‑averaged values of T1 and T2, then calculate the relative temperature on the axis Θ = T1 – T2. If fluctuations are present, select an integer number of oscillation periods at the given speed for the averaging interval.

steps.title: Determine convection threshold
steps.instruction: From the Θ versus rotation‑speed plot, identify the threshold velocity (boundary between regions I and II) and note the corresponding T1, T2 and Θ values.

steps.title: Compute thermophysical properties
steps.instruction: For each step, calculate density, viscosity, coefficient of volumetric expansion and thermal conductivity at the average temperature T = (T1 + T2)/2; use these values when forming dimensionless groups.

steps.title: Note power density (no‑vibration case)
steps.instruction: The power density for the heat‑generating fluid in this set of experiments is 0.087 W · cm⁻³.

steps.title: Convection experiment with transverse vibrations
steps.instruction: Perform a second series of experiments in which the rotating cavity (2–4 rps) is subjected to transverse vibrations.

steps.title: Prepare rotating, heated cuvette
steps.instruction: Bring the cuvette to a fast rotation of 2, 3, or 4 rps, turn the heating on, and wait until a steady‑state temperature distribution is established (same criteria as before).

steps.title: Apply transverse vibrations
steps.instruction: Activate the mechanical vibrator with a fixed amplitude of b = 24.57 mm and a vibration frequency that initially exceeds the rotation frequency.

steps.title: Decrease vibration frequency stepwise
steps.instruction: Reduce the vibration frequency in discrete steps, monitoring T1 and T2 in real time at each step.

steps.title: Wait for stationary convection after each step
steps.instruction: Proceed to the next vibration frequency only after a stationary convection mode has been reached (minimum 15 min).

steps.title: Repeat at different vibration amplitudes
steps.instruction: Conduct the above frequency‑step series for several chosen vibration amplitudes.

steps.title: Observe temperature response
steps.instruction: When the vibration frequency differs markedly from the rotation frequency, T1 and T2 remain constant within the meter accuracy of 0.1 °C; when the frequencies are close, a decrease of T1 (cooling of the cavity centre) is observed.

steps.title: Note power density (vibration case)
steps.instruction: The power density for the vibrating‑cavity experiments is 0.027 W · cm⁻³.
